# 🏠 Flatfinder — download one file and run it

No install, no account, no Python, no coding. Scroll down to **Assets**, grab the file for your computer, and follow the three steps below.

| Your computer | Download |
|---|---|
| **Windows** | `Flatfinder-windows.exe` |
| **Mac** | `Flatfinder-macos.zip` |

## Windows — first time

1. Download **`Flatfinder-windows.exe`** (under **Assets** below).
2. Move it into its own folder — e.g. make a folder called `Flatfinder` in Documents and drop it in. It keeps your settings in that folder, next to itself.
3. **Double-click it.** If Windows shows *“Windows protected your PC”*, click **More info → Run anyway**. That warning appears for any free unsigned download — it doesn't mean something is wrong.
4. Be patient for ~15 seconds on the first start (it unpacks itself) — a window will appear.
5. Answer **3 questions** — your work postcode, budget, and max commute — and it starts hunting. When it offers to put a **shortcut on your Desktop**, say yes.

## Mac — first time

1. Download **`Flatfinder-macos.zip`** (under **Assets** below) and double-click the zip to unpack it.
2. **Right-click** the unpacked **`Flatfinder`** → **Open** → **Open**. (Needed once — Macs block unsigned apps on plain double-click the first time.)
3. Answer the **3 questions** — done.

## Every time after

Just double-click **Flatfinder** (or your Desktop shortcut). Each run only shows rooms that are **new since last time** — no re-scrolling the same flats. When a new version comes out, the app **tells you when it starts** — press **9** and it fetches the update for you; you never need to come back to this page.

---

*What is this? Flatfinder searches SpareRoom and keeps only the rooms with a real door-to-door commute (walk → tube/bus/rail → walk) under your limit, using Transport for London's journey planner — then opens the new matches in your browser. More at the [project README](https://github.com/TonyClone/spareroom-commute-finder#readme).*
